verdicts.quote: "BigCommerce uses a modified version of the OAuth2 authorization code grant."
verdicts.reason: Public apps install via OAuth code grant and receive a per‑store access_token, which is the standard multi‑tenant flow. ([docs.bigcommerce.com](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/integrations/apps/guide/auth))

verdicts.quote: "You can create and install draft apps without being a BigCommerce partner… To make the app available to other stores, submit it for approval."
verdicts.reason: Dev creds are self‑serve for drafts, but production distribution to other stores requires Marketplace review — fits app_review. ([docs.bigcommerce.com](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/integrations/apps/guide/types-of-apps))

verdicts.quote: "What’s inside: … Catalog … Content … Management — Orders, Customers, Shipping … Payments … Webhooks."
verdicts.reason: The Admin APIs cover dozens of resources across most product areas, indicating broad scope. ([docs.bigcommerce.com](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/rest/admin/overview))

verdicts.quote: "BigCommerce supports MCP in three ways… Storefront MCP … Generally available … Store Management MCP … Early access."
verdicts.reason: These are vendor‑operated MCP servers documented by BigCommerce, not community projects. ([docs.bigcommerce.com](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/mcp/overview/))

verdicts.quote: "You don’t need to be a partner to build and test an app… You need an approved Technology Partner account to submit an app to the BigCommerce App Marketplace."
verdicts.reason: To ship an OAuth app other stores can install, Composio would need partner acceptance/review; otherwise limited to own stores. ([docs.bigcommerce.com](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/integrations/becoming-a-partner))
